candidates.source_name: Payten Montenegro (Asseco Group) - corporate news & Montenegro country page
candidates.why_relevant: Payten is described in Montenegrin-market material as the leading ATM/POS provider in Montenegro, present since 2006, with long-term relationships with 9 of ~11 banks, 28 staff locally. Its news feed publishes bank-by-bank implementation announcements (e.g. SoftPOS at Hipotekarna banka), which simultaneously reveal a Montenegrin bank project and Payten's own local organisational build-out.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic crawl of the news index filtered for 'Montenegro/Crna Gora/Podgorica' plus named ME banks; snapshot customer/reference mentions.
candidates.discovered_via_method: en vendor-side search then snowball from MFIC member profile
queries_used: Payten Montenegro POS ATM banks partner

candidates.source_name: Montenegrin Foreign Investors Council (MFIC) - member profile pages (Payten and other vendors)
candidates.why_relevant: MFIC member profiles carry unusually concrete Montenegro-specific vendor facts: local headcount, number of ATMs/POS deployed, number of bank customers, year of market entry. It is also an actor map for which international suppliers actually have a registered Montenegrin presence, and members' representatives are named, which surfaces country-manager-level people.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Enumerate member list, diff membership over time (new member = new local entity), scrape member profile text for headcount and customer claims.
candidates.discovered_via_method: search result snowball from Payten query
queries_used: Payten Montenegro POS ATM banks partner

candidates.source_name: Printec Montenegro - country page (Printec Group)
candidates.why_relevant: Printec Montenegro (present since 2014) publishes its local footprint: ~15+ staff, service centres in Podgorica, Ulcinj, Budva, Herceg Novi, and team functions (Business Development, Sales, Customer Support, Professional Services). Changes to this page are a direct signal of local office openings, headcount growth and function build-out in the transaction-automation supplier layer serving ME banks.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Change-detection snapshot of the country page plus the group careers/news sections filtered for Montenegro.
queries_used: Printec Montenegro Podgorica banks ATM services office

candidates.source_name: Logate (Podgorica) - customer/reference and CX360 banking product pages
candidates.why_relevant: Domestic Podgorica software vendor that publicly names its Montenegrin bank customers for its banking CRM (Erste Montenegro, NLB Podgorica, CKB/OTP, Hipotekarna, Lovcen banka, Prva banka, AIK). Reference-page changes reveal new bank projects; the About/careers pages reveal headcount and hiring in the bank-facing delivery teams.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Snapshot /cx360/, /about-us/ and careers pages; diff the named-customer logo/name list.
candidates.discovered_via_method: en vendor search, snowballed from Montenegro IT-cluster results
queries_used: Logate Podgorica banking software company Montenegro clients

candidates.source_name: Logate LinkedIn company page (me.linkedin.com)
candidates.why_relevant: Vendor LinkedIn pages are the fastest-moving indicator of hires, new roles and leadership announcements in the Montenegrin bank-supplier layer; the .me subdomain confirms Montenegro registration.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual analyst review, or licensed data (LinkedIn Talent/Sales Navigator, or a compliant vendor feed). Do not scrape.
queries_used: Logate Podgorica banking software company Montenegro clients
candidates.observed_blocker: LinkedIn requires login for most company/people views and prohibits automated collection

candidates.source_name: ICT Cortex - Montenegrin ICT cluster (member directory, news, open positions)
candidates.why_relevant: Cluster of ~40 Montenegrin ICT companies; publishes member profiles, aggregated open positions of member companies and business-performance analyses. It is the single best actor map for domestic integrators that could be serving banks, and its job-openings posts are a hiring signal aggregator.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl member directory pages plus the news feed; snowball each member to its own careers/reference pages.
queries_used: ICT Cortex Crna Gora clanice IT kompanije klaster spisak

candidates.source_name: Asseco SEE / Asseco group Montenegro-facing products (NLB Klik / ProKlik ME mobile apps, Google Play listings)
candidates.why_relevant: Play Store package names expose the vendor behind a Montenegrin bank's digital channel (e.g. NLB Montenegro apps published under Asseco package namespaces). This is a reliable indirect way to attribute a bank's channel stack to a supplier even when neither party issues a press release; developer/publisher changes signal a vendor switch.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Track package ids, publisher names and release notes for all ME bank apps on Play/App Store; alert on publisher or namespace change.
queries_used: Asseco SEE Crna Gora banka referenca Podgorica

candidates.source_name: Erste Bank AD Podgorica - e-banking platform migration notices (Halcom -> eMon OfficeBanking)
candidates.why_relevant: Customer-facing migration notices on a private bank's own site are one of the few public disclosures of a supplier swap at a Montenegrin bank (here: away from Halcom's platform to an OfficeBanking-family product). Such projects reliably accompany internal reorganisation and vendor-side hiring.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor the eBankarstvo/obavjestenja sections of all ME bank sites for platform-migration and 'nova aplikacija' notices; extract named product/vendor.
candidates.discovered_via_method: sr search on vendor name + Crna Gora
queries_used: Halcom Crna Gora banke e-banking dobavljac Podgorica

candidates.source_name: Halcom - bank coverage / supported-banks pages and regional site
candidates.why_relevant: Halcom publicly states it operates across seven monetary systems including Montenegro and lists partner banks; its bank lists and CA (certification) pages let you attribute corporate e-banking and e-signature infrastructure at ME banks, and detect losses of customers (as at Erste ME).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Snapshot supported-bank listings per country; diff for additions/removals of Montenegrin banks.
queries_used: Halcom Crna Gora banke e-banking dobavljac Podgorica

candidates.source_name: Poslovi Infostud - regional job board carrying ME/regional vendor vacancies (e.g. Payten ATM technician)
candidates.why_relevant: Vendor vacancies (ATM tehnicar at Payten d.o.o., POS field service, implementation consultants) are the most granular public evidence of a supplier scaling a Montenegro/regional service organisation. Job text often names the bank programme or terminal estate being supported.
candidates.legal_status: public listings; check ToS before bulk crawl
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword-scheduled queries on employer names (Payten, Printec, Asseco, Halcom, NCR, Diebold) plus location filters; archive ad text since ads expire.

candidates.why_relevant: Described as the most-visited Montenegrin employment portal; the IT category is where a vendor opening a Podgorica office or country-manager role would advertise locally.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Daily category crawl with employer-name and keyword matching ('country manager', 'predstavnistvo', 'banka', 'POS', 'bankomat').

candidates.source_name: Radnik.me - Montenegrin job portal, Podgorica listings
candidates.why_relevant: Second Montenegrin job aggregator; redundancy matters because vendor ads are posted unevenly across ME portals and expire quickly.

candidates.source_name: Prekoveze.me - Montenegrin employment site (Podgorica ads)
candidates.why_relevant: Additional ME-domestic vacancy source described as a leading employment site in Montenegro; useful for SME integrators and field-service roles that never reach LinkedIn.

candidates.source_name: Berza rada - Montenegrin employment portal with employer profile pages
candidates.why_relevant: Hosts per-employer profile pages ('poslodavci/...'), which give a persistent handle for tracking a given vendor's hiring cadence in Montenegro rather than only single ads.

queries_used: oglas za posao Podgorica IT kompanija banke POS ATM tehnicar zaposlenje portal poslovi

candidates.source_name: CRPS - Central Register of Business Entities of Montenegro (company search)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative registry for a foreign vendor incorporating a Montenegrin subsidiary or registering a branch/representative office ('predstavnistvo stranog drustva'), and for changes of executive director. This is the hardest evidence of a supplier 'opening a Podgorica office' and of who its legal representative (de facto country manager) is.
candidates.access_status: public search portal; legacy http, form-based, likely no bulk API
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Named-entity lookups for a vendor watchlist; periodic re-query for status/representative changes. Treat as a confirmation layer for signals found on vendor sites.
queries_used: CRPS Crna Gora registar privrednih subjekata pretraga predstavnistvo stranog drustva

candidates.source_name: eUprava Montenegro - business registration service pages
candidates.why_relevant: Explains the registration procedures and the exact legal form names used for foreign presence in Montenegro, which supplies the correct query vocabulary for CRPS lookups and for spotting a vendor's first legal footprint.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off read to build glossary; re-check when procedures change.
queries_used: CRPS Crna Gora registar privrednih subjekata pretraga predstavnistvo stranog drustva

negative_findings.description: Searched in both English and Serbian for evidence of Diebold Nixdorf or NCR Atleos activity, contracts, offices or hires in Montenegro.
negative_findings.result_summary: No Montenegro-specific page, press release or local entity for either global ATM OEM was found; results were generic global ATM-industry articles. Their ME footprint appears to be routed through partners/distributors (e.g. Payten, Printec) rather than own local entities.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Means direct OEM monitoring is low-yield for ME; the partner/service-provider layer is the correct collection point for ATM estate signals.

negative_findings.description: Searched for a Montenegrin card-personalisation bureau and for named card-personalisation suppliers to Montenegrin banks (sr terms: 'personalizacija platnih kartica', 'dobavljac').
negative_findings.result_summary: Only Serbia-based personalisation providers (Zeta, SIS, Cards Print) surfaced, plus ME bank card terms-and-conditions PDFs. No Montenegrin personalisation bureau and no explicit ME bank-supplier pairing was found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Card personalisation for ME banks is likely regional or in-house; the cell's card-personalisation sub-question cannot be answered from ME-domestic sources and needs regional vendor monitoring instead.

negative_findings.description: Searched for an explicit 'core banking' vendor-to-Montenegrin-bank attribution (which core system each ME bank runs) in en and sr.
negative_findings.result_summary: No public attribution found via general search. Montenegrin systemic banks are private and mostly foreign-group subsidiaries, so core-system choices are made at group level and not disclosed locally.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale: core-banking procurement is invisible; indirect proxies (mobile-app package namespaces, e-banking migration notices, CRM reference pages, job ads naming systems) are the only viable route.

negative_findings.description: General web search repeatedly returned Wikipedia bank stubs and CBCG register pages for vendor-oriented queries in both languages.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bank-name tokens dominate ranking, crowding out supplier content. Productive results only came from vendor-name-anchored queries (Payten, Printec, Logate, Halcom, Asseco) and portal-name-anchored queries.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design should be entity-anchored (vendor watchlist) rather than topic-anchored keyword search.

negative_findings.description: LinkedIn (me.linkedin.com company and jobs pages) and EMIS company profiles are the richest people/appointment sources identified.
negative_findings.result_summary: LinkedIn is auth-walled and its ToS forbids automated collection; EMIS is subscription-paywalled. Neither was collected.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single best leadership-move signal for this cell is not lawfully machine-collectable without licensing; budget for licensed access or manual analyst review.

negative_findings.description: Attempted to locate the Chamber of Economy of Montenegro ICT/banking board membership pages in Serbian.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search surfaced only the chamber's supervisory board and contact pages, not an ICT board membership list; the page may exist but was not reachable via search.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Recorded as unverified rather than absent; needs manual site navigation before concluding the source does not exist.

coverage_gaps.description: No confirmed source found for the Montenegro presence of major international core-banking/payments vendors beyond the Asseco/Payten and Printec families (e.g. Temenos, Oracle FSS, Finastra, BPC, OpenWay, Nets/Nexi, Worldline, Idemia, Thales).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run an entity-anchored second pass: for each vendor on a fixed watchlist, query '<vendor> Crna Gora', '<vendor> Podgorica', '<vendor> Montenegro' and check the vendor's own customers/press pages and CRPS for a ME entity.

coverage_gaps.description: No people-level appointment source is lawfully collectable: no ME equivalent of an executive-appointments wire was identified for the supplier layer.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Combine CRPS legal-representative changes (authoritative, collectable) with Bankar.me appointment items and, if budget allows, licensed LinkedIn/EMIS data.

coverage_gaps.description: ICT Cortex full member directory URL, MFIC full member list URL and the Payten Montenegro local page were inferred from search snippets rather than opened; exact directory paths are unconfirmed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Deterministic liveness/path-resolution pass over ictcortex.me, mfic.me and payten.com to pin the canonical directory and country-page URLs.

coverage_gaps.description: Serbian-language searching used standard ekavian/ijekavian business terms; no Cyrillic-script variants were tried, and Montenegrin-specific orthography (s'/z') was not exercised.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add Cyrillic transliterations of vendor and role terms (банка, представништво, запошљавање, банкомат) to the query set for a follow-up pass.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank-side procurement/tender visibility for private banks was not tested in this cell (public e-procurement covers state bodies only), and no supplier-side tender-award announcements for ME banks were found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Confirm with the workstream owner that CBCG/state procurement is covered by another cell; here, substitute vendor press releases and bank customer-notice pages as the procurement proxy.

brief: Montenegro's private banks disclose almost nothing about their technology suppliers, but the supplier layer is unusually legible: Payten (Asseco) and Printec both publish Montenegro-specific footprint and headcount data and name bank customers, and domestic Podgorica vendors such as Logate list their ME bank references outright. The highest-value monitoring set is therefore vendor newsrooms and reference pages, cross-checked against CRPS (the authoritative record of a foreign vendor incorporating a ME entity or changing its legal representative) and against ME job boards (Zaposli.ME, Radnik.me, Prekoveze.me, Berza rada, Poslovi Infostud), where field-service and country-level roles appear before any press release. Indirect attribution works well here: mobile-banking app package namespaces and customer-facing e-banking migration notices (e.g. Erste ME moving off the Halcom platform) reveal supplier changes that neither party announces. The main structural gaps are people-level appointment data, which sits behind LinkedIn's ToS and EMIS's paywall, and any Montenegrin card-personalisation capability, for which no domestic source was found at all.
